title: Hardware & coil control
heading: Connect your machine's hardware.
intro: Set up switches, coils and lights in one hardware map. Choose output drivers, configure safety limits and send supported settings to the ESP32-S3.
points: Map your connections
Name components, assign functions and choose drivers so your wiring makes sense when you return to the project.
Set safe coil limits
The ESP enforces configured coil pulse and hold limits, cooldowns, arming requirements and watchdogs. Configure limits for your actual coils and drivers.
Configure supported outputs
Use pulse outputs, PWM hold or paired windings where supported. New coil configurations begin disabled with conservative defaults.
seo_title: Pinball Hardware Mapping & ESP32 Coil Control
seo_description: Configure switches, LEDs and coil drivers for your homebrew pinball machine. Map hardware in your browser with coil limits enforced on the ESP32.

title: Rules & scoring
heading: Create the rules for your game.
intro: Choose how your machine responds to switches and events. Build scoring, combinations and multipliers, and run supported fast hardware responses on the ESP32-S3.
points: Connect events to actions
Use the rule editor to connect events, conditions and actions. Keep the logic visible as your machine grows.
Build scoring and combinations
Author scoring rules, combinations and multipliers on the Pi, alongside the rest of your game's configuration.
Keep supported fast responses on the ESP
Deploy supported hardware rules to the ESP. Flipper and simple lighting responses can run locally while scoring and sound are handled on the Pi.
seo_description: Build homebrew pinball rules, scoring combinations and multipliers in your browser. Run supported hardware responses locally on the ESP32.

title: Lighting
heading: Make the playfield part of the story.
intro: Arrange fixtures, design lighting scenes and preview the result before sending it to your machine.
points: Design in context
Position fixtures on a visual stage and build scenes around the layout of your playfield.
From a flash to a scene
Use direct event-driven pixel actions for simple feedback, or compose richer scenes for modes and celebrations.
Preview, then deploy
Test your ideas visually. Compiled lighting files reduce runtime data, while supported ESP rules execute without a duplicate host action.
seo_description: Design LED lighting for your homebrew pinball machine. Arrange fixtures, preview scenes and deploy lighting configurations to the ESP32.

title: Audio & backglass
heading: Give your game a voice. And a world.
intro: Bring together sound cues, media scenes and Godot-powered displays to give each mode its own atmosphere.
points: Sound with intention
Organise audio cues and outputs, and choose how playback behaves when the next event arrives.
A stage for your displays
Compose media scenes and manage displays through the Godot media runtime.
Build beyond the playfield
Develop a backglass scene independently in Godot, then export it for use in your machine's media workflow.
seo_description: Create sound cues and Godot backglass scenes for your homebrew pinball machine. Manage audio, media and displays from one browser interface.

title: Live View
heading: Try the idea before you wire it.
intro: Explore your playfield, trigger configured inputs and watch lighting respond in a visual development workspace.
points: A useful development companion
Use your playfield layout to exercise configured events and inspect how your machine responds.
The connected event path
With an ESP connected, simulated inputs travel through the bridge and firmware before reaching host consumers.
Know what a preview means
Offline authoring and previews help you iterate. They do not replace testing real electrical outputs and hardware timing.
seo_title: Live Pinball Playfield Preview & Event Testing
seo_description: Preview your pinball playfield and exercise configured events in Live View. Follow the bridge event path while developing your homebrew machine.

title: Performance & diagnostics
heading: See what your machine is doing.
intro: Watch event delivery, inspect logs and diagnose the connection between the Pi and ESP without guessing.
points: Follow the traffic
Track incoming events, confirmations, queue depth and delivery latency in the Performance module.
Find the useful signal
Inspect event and service logs without unchanged coil status messages overwhelming the view.
Recover deliberately
Isolated delivery overloads pause activations and recover after cooldown and healthy queues. Repeated overloads and firmware faults remain disarmed.
seo_description: Monitor your pinball controller with event logs, delivery metrics and bridge diagnostics. Investigate Raspberry Pi to ESP32 communication.
